theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: The new board secretary of a statutory body wants the board to cover its budget, audit, strategy and risk reviews at the right times. What should she prepare first?
options: A list of the members' favourite meeting venues across the island
An annual board calendar linking each meeting to its key business
A draft of the minutes for every meeting in the coming year
A plan to hold every meeting online to save on travel costs

questions.stem: Who normally settles the agenda for a meeting of a public body's board?
options: Any member who emails the secretary first with an item
The most senior manager in the finance department alone
The chair, with the CEO and the board secretary
The portfolio ministry's junior staff, by phone

questions.stem: The CEO wants the board to approve the cleaning roster for the head office. What should the secretary advise?
options: Put it first on the agenda, as it affects every member of staff in the building
Put it on the agenda for a vote by the full board next month
Send it to every member for comment by email this week
It is a management matter and does not belong on the board agenda

questions.stem: Which feature most helps board members deal quickly and well with a long paper?
options: A short summary at the front, stating the decision sought and the recommendation
An attractive cover page with the body's logo and colours in full
Every supporting spreadsheet printed in full within the main text
A long history of the issue placed before any of the main points

questions.stem: The board's rules say papers must go out 7 days before a meeting. The meeting is on Thursday 20 March. By when must the papers be sent?
options: Friday 14 March
Thursday 13 March
Monday 17 March
Thursday 6 March

questions.stem: On the morning of the meeting, the CEO hands out a new paper asking the board to approve a J$80,000,000 contract. What is the best response by the chair?
options: Approve it quickly, as the CEO has already done the work
Ask members to read it during the lunch break and then take the vote straight after
Defer the decision unless it is truly urgent and members can judge it
Let the CEO decide, since the paper arrived too late for the board

questions.stem: Why do many boards send their papers through a secure board portal rather than ordinary email?
options: Because email cannot carry files longer than ten pages
Because the law forbids boards from using email at all
Because portals make the papers shorter and easier to write
Because it controls access and protects confidential papers

questions.stem: A board groups routine items, such as noting committee minutes, and approves them together without debate unless a member asks to discuss one. What is this called?
options: A consent agenda
An in-camera session
A written resolution
An extraordinary meeting

questions.stem: A member wants to question an item that has been placed in the consent agenda. What should happen?
options: The member must wait until the next meeting before raising the question at all
The item is taken out of the consent agenda and discussed on its own
The chair rules the question out of order and moves on
The whole consent agenda is withdrawn and cancelled

questions.stem: Why does the board secretary meet the chair a few days before the meeting?
options: To agree in private how each member should be asked to vote on the main items
To write the minutes in advance so they are ready on the day
To go through the agenda, timings, likely issues and any conflicts
To decide which members should not be sent the papers

questions.stem: A board has 9 members. Its rules set the quorum at more than half of the members. What is the quorum?
options: 3 members
4 members
6 members
5 members

questions.stem: At the start time, only four of the nine members have arrived and the quorum is five. What should the chair do?
options: Wait for the time the rules allow, then adjourn if there is still no quorum
Start and make decisions, then ask the absent members to agree later
Let a senior manager sit in as the fifth member for the day
Hold the meeting and mark the absent members as present

questions.stem: Five of nine members are present and the quorum is five. One member declares an interest in item 6 and leaves. Under the board's rules, she does not count towards the quorum for that item. What should happen to item 6?
options: The remaining four decide it, because the meeting began with a quorum present
It is deferred to a quorate meeting or dealt with as the rules allow
The member who left is asked to return and vote on it after all
The chair decides it alone, since the board cannot do so

questions.stem: When should a board meeting normally deal with declarations of interest?
options: Only at the end of the meeting, after the votes are taken
Only when a member of the public complains to the ministry about a possible conflict
Near the start, as a standing item, and again at any item affected
Only once a year, at the meeting that approves the accounts

questions.stem: A member declares an interest and leaves the room for an item. What should the minutes record?
options: Nothing at all, so as to protect the member's privacy and her good reputation
Only that an unnamed member had some kind of interest
The full details of the member's private finances
The member's name, the interest, and when she left and returned

questions.stem: The agenda gives 45 minutes to the five-year strategy, but routine reports have taken the first hour. What should the chair do?
options: Move swiftly to the strategy item and agree how to deal with what is left
Cut the strategy item down to ten minutes so that the meeting ends exactly on time
Keep going through every report in full, whatever the time
End the meeting and leave the strategy for next year

questions.stem: During debate on a major contract, two members argue about a staff matter that is not on the agenda. What should the chair do?
options: Let them continue, as debate shows the board is engaged
Bring the debate back to the item and offer to deal with the other matter properly later
Ask the members to leave the room until they calm down
Call a vote on the staff matter straight away

questions.stem: Senior managers present papers to the board. What is usual practice for their attendance?
options: They stay for the whole meeting and vote on every item alongside the members
They are never allowed into the boardroom at all
They attend for their items, at the chair's invitation, without voting
They take the minutes for the items they present

questions.stem: The board wants to discuss the CEO's performance without management present. What is this part of the meeting usually called?
options: A consent agenda
A written resolution
Matters arising
An in-camera session

questions.stem: How should the record of an in-camera session be handled?
options: Kept as a separate, confidential minute with restricted access
Not recorded at all, so that nothing can be used later
Added to the public minutes with every word spoken
Sent to all staff by email so that they understand the board's view on the matter

questions.stem: Which is the best wording for a board resolution?
options: The board talked about the new office and generally liked the idea.
Resolved: that the board approves the lease of the Mandeville office at the rent in Paper 5, for three years.
The board will think more about the Mandeville office later.
Members were mostly in favour of moving offices in principle.

questions.stem: A decision needs a majority of the members present and voting. Eight are present: 5 vote for, 2 against and 1 abstains. What is the result?
options: It fails, as it needs five of all nine members' votes
It fails, because one member did not vote at all
It passes, with 5 votes for against 2 against
The vote must be held again with all nine members

questions.stem: The board's rules say a change to its standing orders needs two-thirds of all 12 members. How many votes in favour are needed?
A member asks for her vote against a resolution to be recorded. What should the secretary do?
options: Record in the minutes that she voted against
Refuse, as the minutes show only the result
Record it only if the chair agrees with her view
Leave her off the attendance list for that item

questions.stem: During debate, a member proposes a change to the wording of a resolution. In most standing orders, what happens next?
options: The original resolution is voted on first, and the change afterwards
The amendment is debated and voted on before the main resolution
The chair decides alone whether to accept the change
The resolution is withdrawn and brought back next year

questions.stem: An urgent decision is needed two weeks before the next meeting, and the rules allow decisions by written resolution. What must happen?
options: The chair signs the decision alone on behalf of the board
The CEO decides and tells the board at its next meeting
Every member gets the paper, signs as the rules require, and it is reported at the next meeting
Only the members who live in Kingston are asked to sign it

questions.stem: A hurricane has damaged the body's main office and decisions are needed this week that need debate. What is usually the best route?
options: Wait for the next ordinary meeting in two months' time
Let the CEO take every decision without telling the board
Ask one member to decide on behalf of the whole board
Call a special or extraordinary meeting under the rules

questions.stem: The chair is ill on the day of the meeting. What normally happens?
options: The deputy chair presides, or members choose a chair for the meeting as the rules say
The CEO chairs the meeting in place of the chair
The meeting goes ahead with no one in the chair
The board secretary chairs and votes

questions.stem: A board plans to hold some meetings by video link. What should be confirmed first?
options: That members can switch off their cameras for the whole meeting
That the rules allow it, and members can hear each other, take part and keep it confidential
That every member owns the same type of laptop
That the meeting is streamed live on social media

questions.stem: The secretary wants to make an audio recording of board meetings to help write minutes. What should she do?
options: Record secretly so that members speak freely
Record and share the file with all staff
Follow the board's policy, tell members, and keep or delete the file as it says
Record only the members she thinks will be difficult, and keep the files at home

questions.stem: What is the main role of the board secretary at the meeting itself?
options: To lead the debate on each item and sum it up
To vote when the board is evenly split
To present every management paper
To advise on procedure, record attendance, decisions and actions

questions.stem: During a meeting, the chair proposes to approve an item that the rules say must go first to the audit committee. What should the secretary do?
options: Politely advise the chair of the rule and the options
Say nothing, as the chair outranks the secretary
Leave the meeting in protest
Change the minutes later to show it went to the committee

questions.stem: How should the audit committee normally report to the full board?
options: Only when the external auditor asks it to report
By a short report of its work, findings and any recommendations for decision
By repeating the whole of its own meeting, item by item, in front of the full board
By sending its draft minutes to staff

questions.stem: What should the minutes of a board meeting mainly contain?
options: Every word spoken by every member and every manager, in full and in order
Only the names of those who attended
Decisions, key reasons, resolutions and actions, with who and when
The secretary's own opinion of each debate

questions.stem: Why are board resolutions often given a reference number, such as 2026/14?
options: So the board can vote on them by number only
So that members do not need to read them
So that they can be kept secret from the auditors and the portfolio ministry
So each decision can be found, cited and tracked later

questions.stem: How are the minutes of a board meeting normally made official?
options: They are confirmed at the next meeting and signed by the chair
They are approved by the CEO the day after the meeting
They become official as soon as the secretary has typed and printed them
They are approved by the portfolio ministry's staff

questions.stem: Why should the minutes record the paper reference for each item the board decides?
options: So that members need not read the papers before the next meeting
So the decision is linked to the information the board relied on
So that the paper can be thrown away once the minutes are written
So that the secretary can leave the reasons out of the minutes

questions.stem: Where should the signed minutes and board resolutions be kept?
options: In the chair's home, for safe keeping
In each member's personal email folder
In a secure, controlled minute book or records system
In a box in the staff kitchen

questions.stem: The board approves a new procurement policy. What should happen next?
options: Nothing until the minutes are confirmed at the next meeting in two months' time
Members tell staff about it informally
The policy waits until the next strategy review
The secretary sends the decision to management to act on, with any deadline

questions.stem: How should the board know whether its decisions are being carried out?
options: A schedule of actions, updated by the secretary and reviewed at each meeting
Members visit offices to check without telling management
The chair asks the CEO informally now and then whether things are moving along
The board waits for the external audit each year

questions.stem: Over 10 meetings, a 9-member board recorded 72 attendances. What was the board's overall attendance rate?
A representative of the portfolio ministry asks to attend a board meeting. What should the secretary check?
options: Whether the representative will bring refreshments or expect lunch to be provided
Whether the representative agrees with the CEO
What the rules allow, and whether the chair agrees, for which items
Whether the representative can vote on the budget

questions.stem: A citizen requests copies of a public body's board minutes. How should the request be handled?
options: Refuse at once, as all board minutes are always secret
Release everything, including in-camera minutes, the same day
Ignore it, as citizens may not ask public bodies for records
Deal with it under the access to information rules, with any lawful exemptions

questions.stem: At the end of each meeting, a chair asks members for two minutes of feedback on how the meeting went. What is the main benefit?
options: It helps the board improve its papers, time use and debate
It replaces the need for minutes
It lets members change decisions that were already made earlier in the meeting
It gives members a chance to leave early

questions.stem: After a meeting, several members leave printed confidential papers on the boardroom table. What should the secretary do?
options: Leave them for the cleaners to throw away
Collect them and file or shred them securely, as the policy says
Post them back to members by ordinary mail
Put them in the staff room for others to read

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What two-word term names the group of routine board items approved together without debate unless a member asks to discuss one?
What two-word Latin phrase describes a private part of a board meeting held without management or the public present?
What two-word term names a decision made between meetings when members sign their agreement on a paper, where the rules allow it?
What title is usually given to the officer who manages board papers, advises on procedure and keeps the minutes? (Two words.)
What word names a board meeting called outside the normal calendar to deal with urgent business? (One word, before 'meeting'.)
What two-word term names the short opening section of a board paper that states the issue, the decision sought and the recommendation?

A board's quorum is five. Seven members are present. Three declare an interest in one item and leave, and the rules say they do not count for that item. How many members count towards the quorum for it?
What two-word term names a board's written rules on how its meetings are called, run and recorded?
Board papers must go out 10 days before a meeting on 25 June. On what date must they go out?
Over 6 meetings, an 8-member board recorded 42 attendances. What was its attendance rate, to the nearest whole per cent?
What two-word term names the secure online system many boards use to send papers and keep records?
What title is usually given to the member who presides when the chair is absent? (One or two words.)
What two-word term names the yearly schedule that sets out each board meeting and the main business to be taken at it?
What two-word term names the bound or electronic record that holds a board's signed minutes over the years?
What one-word term names a formal decision of the board, recorded in the minutes, often starting 'Resolved that…'?

essays.stem: As board secretary of a statutory body, explain how you would plan the board's year of meetings so that it covers all its main duties.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start by listing what the board must do in a year under the law that set up the body, its rules and the government's guidance for public bodies: approve the corporate plan and budget, approve the audited financial statements and annual report by their deadlines, review performance each quarter, review risks, appoint and appraise the CEO, review policies, and receive committee reports. I would work with the chair and CEO to set the number of ordinary meetings, for example ten, and fix their dates for the whole year, avoiding public holidays and linking them to the financial year and reporting deadlines. I would then build an annual board calendar showing which items come to which meeting, so that, for example, the draft budget comes in time for submission to the ministry and the accounts arrive after the audit. I would schedule committee meetings before the board meetings they report to. I would add a strategy session, a board evaluation and member training. The calendar would be approved by the board and reviewed mid-year.
markingPoints: Lists the board's yearly duties from the law, rules and guidance
Agrees the number and dates of meetings with chair and CEO
Builds a calendar linking items to meetings and deadlines
Schedules committees before the board meetings they report to
Includes strategy, evaluation and training; approved and reviewed

essays.stem: Describe the standard you would set for board papers, and explain how it helps the board make good decisions.
essays.modelAnswer: Every paper would use a set template. The front page would give the title, the author and the executive responsible, the purpose (for decision, for discussion or for noting), and an executive summary of no more than one page stating the issue, the options, the recommendation and the exact decision sought. The body would set out the background briefly, the analysis of options, the costs and how they will be funded, the risks, legal and policy points, and the link to the strategy. Detail would go into appendices. Papers would have numbered paragraphs, plain language and no unexplained terms, and would usually be no longer than ten pages. Each paper would be checked by the CEO and reach me by a set deadline, so that the whole pack can go out seven days before the meeting through the board portal. This standard helps because members can see quickly what they are asked to decide and why, can prepare properly, and can challenge on facts rather than guesswork. It also makes the minutes and later audits easier.
markingPoints: Template with purpose and executive summary stating the decision sought
Covers options, costs, risks, legal points and link to strategy
Clear presentation: plain language, numbered paragraphs, appendices, length limit
Internal checks, deadlines and secure distribution in good time
Explains how the standard improves preparation and decisions

essays.stem: Plan the board secretary's tasks before, during and after a board meeting.
essays.modelAnswer: Before the meeting I would draft the agenda with the chair and CEO, using the annual calendar and the action schedule, and send the notice as the rules require. I would chase papers by the internal deadline, check them against the template, and send the full pack securely seven days ahead. I would confirm attendance and apologies, check that a quorum is likely, book the room or video link, and update the register of interests. I would brief the chair on the agenda, timings and any likely conflicts. During the meeting I would record attendance and confirm the quorum, call for declarations of interest, advise the chair on procedure when needed, note who leaves and returns, and record decisions, resolutions, votes where needed and actions with owners and dates. After the meeting I would send decisions to management straight away, draft the minutes within a few days for the chair to review, update the action schedule, file the papers and confidential minutes securely, and collect or shred spare papers. The draft minutes go to the next meeting for confirmation.
markingPoints: Before: agenda, notice, papers checked and sent on time
Before: attendance, quorum, venue, register and chair's briefing
During: quorum, declarations, procedural advice, accurate record
After: decisions sent to management, draft minutes to chair, action schedule
After: secure filing and confirmation of minutes at next meeting

essays.stem: A board of nine has a quorum of five. Six members attend. Two members declare interests in a contract item and, under the rules, must leave and do not count towards the quorum for it. Explain what the chair and secretary should do.
essays.modelAnswer: At the start, six members are present, so the meeting is quorate. When declarations of interest are called, the secretary should record both members' declarations, with the nature of each interest, in the minutes. When the contract item is reached, the two members must leave. That leaves four members, below the quorum of five, and because the conflicted members do not count for this item, the board cannot make a valid decision on it. The chair should not let the four remaining members decide anyway, because the decision could be challenged and set aside. The secretary should advise the chair of the rule and the options. These usually include deferring the item to a later meeting at which more members without conflicts will attend, calling a special meeting, or using a written resolution of the members who have no conflict, if the rules allow it. The minutes should record that the two members left, that the item could not be decided for lack of a quorum, and what was agreed instead. The rest of the agenda can continue once the members return.
markingPoints: Recognises the meeting is quorate at the start (six of nine)
Records both declarations and the members leaving
Works out that four remain, below the quorum for that item
Does not decide the item; secretary advises on options (defer, special meeting, written resolution if allowed)
Minutes record what happened; rest of the agenda continues

essays.stem: The board must decide whether to close two rural offices, and members and management hold strong views. Explain how the chair should manage this item.
essays.modelAnswer: Before the meeting, the chair should make sure the paper sets out the options, costs, effects on service and staff, consultation results and risks, and that it reaches members in good time. She should place the item early on the agenda and give it enough time. At the meeting she should introduce the item by stating what the board is asked to decide and remind members to declare any interests. She should invite management to present briefly, then let members ask questions of fact before debate. During debate she should bring in every member, especially quieter ones, keep the discussion on the evidence and on the board's duty to the public, and stop personal attacks. If new facts are needed, she can propose deferring the decision. When views are clear, she should sum up the main points and the proposal, and check whether consensus is possible, perhaps with conditions such as mobile services. If not, she should take a vote under the rules, and ensure that the resolution and any recorded dissent are minuted clearly.
markingPoints: Ensures a full, balanced paper in good time and places the item early
Opens by stating the decision sought and calling for declarations
Structures: management presentation, questions of fact, then debate
Includes all members, keeps to evidence and stops personal attacks
Sums up, seeks consensus or votes, and records the resolution and dissent

essays.stem: Explain how you would write the minutes of a board meeting so that they are accurate, clear and useful as a legal record.
essays.modelAnswer: I would follow the agenda's order and numbering, and begin with the name of the body, the date, time and place, the members present, apologies, others in attendance and for which items, and confirmation of the quorum. I would record every declaration of interest and when members left and returned. For each item I would give the paper reference, a brief summary of the main points and the reasons for the decision, without recording who said every word. Decisions would be written as numbered resolutions in exact words, for example 'Resolved (2026/14): that the board approves…', with votes recorded where the rules require or a member asks. Actions would show the owner and the due date. I would write in the past tense, neutrally and concisely, and avoid opinions. Confidential or in-camera items would be minuted separately with restricted access. I would draft the minutes within a few days, check facts with presenters, and send them to the chair. Once confirmed at the next meeting and signed, they become the official record, kept securely.
markingPoints: Header details, attendance, apologies and quorum
Declarations of interest and movements recorded
Summary of main points and reasons, not verbatim
Numbered resolutions in exact words, votes where needed, actions with owners and dates
Neutral style, separate confidential minutes, prompt drafting, confirmation and secure keeping

essays.stem: Compare using a written resolution with calling an extraordinary meeting for an urgent decision, and recommend when each should be used.
essays.modelAnswer: A written resolution is a paper sent to all members that becomes a decision when the required number sign, if the rules allow it. It is quick and cheap and suits a clear, simple matter on which members are likely to agree, such as approving a bank signatory change or a contract already discussed. Its weakness is that there is no debate, so members cannot question management together or hear each other's views, and conflicts of interest are harder to manage. It must be sent to every member and reported at the next meeting. An extraordinary meeting is called at short notice under the rules, in person or by video link. It takes more effort and may struggle to reach a quorum, but it allows full discussion, questions and amendment, which suits complex or sensitive matters, such as decisions after a hurricane or a serious financial problem. I would recommend a written resolution for simple, urgent, uncontested matters, and an extraordinary meeting whenever the decision is significant, uncertain or needs debate.
markingPoints: Explains the written resolution and its rules (all members, signatures, reported later)
Strengths and weaknesses of the written resolution
Explains the extraordinary meeting and its strengths and weaknesses
Gives suitable examples for each
Makes a clear recommendation on when to use each

essays.stem: Justify why a board should sometimes meet in camera, and explain how such sessions should be managed.
essays.modelAnswer: Some matters need frank discussion without management present. Examples include the CEO's performance and pay, a complaint about a senior manager, a legal claim, or the board's own effectiveness. Members may not speak openly if the people concerned are in the room, and some information is too sensitive to share widely. A short in-camera session at the end of each meeting can also make it normal, so that management does not assume something is wrong when one is held. However, in-camera sessions must not be used to avoid accountability. They should be limited to matters that truly need privacy, be on the agenda as an item, and be chaired in the usual way. The board secretary, or another person the rules allow, should usually stay to record decisions, unless the item concerns the secretary. A separate confidential minute should record decisions and reasons, kept with restricted access. Any decision that management must act on should be passed to the right person promptly, and decisions should be reported in the public minutes where possible.
markingPoints: Gives suitable reasons and examples for in-camera sessions
Notes the value of a routine short session
Limits use to matters that need privacy; not to avoid accountability
Placed on the agenda, chaired normally, recorded in a confidential minute
Decisions passed on promptly and reported publicly where possible

essays.stem: Describe a system to make sure board decisions are carried out, and explain how the board should use it.
essays.modelAnswer: Straight after each meeting, the secretary would send management a list of the decisions and actions, with the resolution number, the owner and the due date, so that work can start before the minutes are confirmed. All actions would go into a single schedule of actions, kept by the secretary, showing the meeting, the action, the owner, the due date and the status, such as done, on track or late, with a short comment. Management would update the status before each meeting, and the secretary would check it against the papers. The schedule would be a standing item on every agenda. The board would review late or overdue items, ask why and agree new dates, and remove completed actions once members are satisfied. Large decisions, such as a new policy or a project, would also have a report back at an agreed date, showing results. The chair should press for completion without stepping into management. The audit committee may test, from time to time, whether key decisions were carried out as recorded.
markingPoints: Decisions and actions sent to management promptly after the meeting
A single action schedule with owner, date and status
Management updates and secretary checks before each meeting
Board reviews the schedule as a standing item and challenges delays
Report-backs on major decisions and occasional assurance checks

essays.stem: Members of a public body's board complain that meetings run for five hours and papers arrive late. Plan how you would evaluate and improve the board's meetings.
essays.modelAnswer: I would gather evidence first. I would review the last six agendas, minutes and papers to see how long each item took, how much time went on routine reports compared with strategy and decisions, when papers were sent, and how long they were. I would ask members, with a short confidential survey, what works and what does not, and talk to the chair and CEO. From this I would identify causes, for example, too many items for noting, long papers with no summaries, internal deadlines that are not enforced, and debate that strays. I would then propose changes to the chair and board: an annual calendar to spread business; a consent agenda for routine items; a paper template with a one-page executive summary and a length limit; firm internal deadlines and a rule that late papers are taken only if urgent; timed agendas with strategy items early; and a brief review at the end of each meeting. After three meetings I would measure the results: meeting length, papers on time and members' views, and report them to the board.
markingPoints: Gathers evidence from records and a confidential member survey
Identifies the causes of long meetings and late papers
Proposes changes to agenda: calendar, consent agenda, timed agenda
Proposes changes to papers: template, summary, length limit, deadlines and late-paper rule
Measures the results and reports to the board

practical1.title: Prepare the meeting pack for a public body's board meeting
practical1.brief: Your group is the board secretariat of a made-up public body (the assessor gives you its rules: number of members, quorum, notice period and paper deadline, plus a list of business for the next meeting). Prepare the full meeting pack. Give each member a named role: board secretary (notice, agenda and timings, checking the pack against the rules), paper writer for a decision item (for example, approving a new lease), paper writer for a discussion item (for example, a quarterly performance report), committee officer (a short audit committee report to the board and the consent agenda), and in a group of five a chair's adviser (a one-page chair's brief and an updated register of interests). The agenda must include a consent agenda, a declarations item and a timed order with decision items early. Each paper must use the same template, with an executive summary and the decision sought. Present the pack to the assessor as if to the chair, each member explaining their part.
materials: Assessor's pack: the body's rules and the list of business
Computer with word processor and printer, or paper and pens
Board paper template and agenda template
Calendar for working out notice dates
Folder or envelope for the finished pack
photos: The notice of meeting showing the date worked out from the notice rule
The timed agenda with the consent agenda and declarations item
The decision paper with its executive summary and proposed resolution
The discussion paper and the audit committee report
The chair's brief, the register of interests and the group presenting the pack
checklist: Carried out a named role and produced their own part of the pack
Notice and paper dates are worked out correctly from the rules
Agenda is timed, places decisions early and includes a consent agenda and declarations
Papers follow the template, with a clear executive summary and decision sought
Chair's brief identifies likely issues, conflicts and quorum risks
Explained their part clearly and answered the assessor's questions
safety: Use the made-up body and names only; no real board documents
Mark confidential papers clearly and collect all printed copies at the end
Share the work fairly and help members who finish later
Take a short screen break each hour

practical2.title: Run and minute a board meeting with a declared interest and a vote
practical2.brief: Your group holds a 40-minute role-played board meeting of a made-up public body, using a meeting pack from the assessor (or the pack from Practical 1). Give each member a named role: chair, board secretary (advises on procedure and takes the minutes), CEO (presents the decision paper and leaves for the in-camera item), and board members, one of whom has an interest in an item (the assessor gives this on a sealed card). The meeting must include: confirming the quorum; declarations of interest, with the conflicted member leaving for the item; a consent agenda; debate and a vote on a resolution, with any dissent recorded; and a short in-camera item without the CEO. After the meeting, the secretary drafts the minutes with numbered resolutions and an action schedule, the chair checks and signs them, and every member writes a short note on one thing that went well and one to improve. In a group of four, the assessor plays one board member. Photograph each stage.
materials: Meeting pack from the assessor or from Practical 1
